story: Closing the parenthesis (or ending the heading line) at the end of a guidebook listing's practical details such as opening hours, prices, and web addresses.
Predicting the article 'the' (or 'a') immediately after a preposition like 'of', 'to', 'in', 'at', 'from' in ordinary prose.
Continuing a long word from its first subword chunk, most often British place and proper names like Limehouse, Belgravia, Marylebone, Saxon, Pancras.
Predicting the digits of prices and opening times in listing details, e.g. the '50' in £2.50 or the '4' in 11am-4pm.

Finishing formulaic listing boilerplate that repeats throughout the guide, such as 'GOOGLE MAP', '.co.uk' web suffixes and am/pm hour endings, by copying earlier occurrences, plus some 'of' after quantity phrases like 'one of' or 'view of'.
Predicting a comma right after a noun phrase whose head word already occurred earlier in the passage (e.g. 'at both stations,', 'the public heart of London,').
Completing familiar two-token collocations in guidebook text, like 'Apr-Sep', 'adult/child', 'higher education', 'opening hours'.
Predicting common function words that continue mid-sentence prose after verbs and prepositions ('one of the best', 'easy to get', 'is warmed by the').
Closing a paired delimiter - parenthesis, bold '**', italic '_' or quote - right after the name or title that the matching opener introduced earlier.
Completing weekday ranges in opening hours, above all predicting 'Fri' after the hyphen in 'Mon-Fri'.
At the start of a venue's details line: right after the name-plus-category header, predicting the opening '(' of the phone/map/website block that every listing repeats.
Predicting the day-of-week name at the end of an opening-hours clause, e.g. 'to 10.30pm Sun' or '8am-9pm Sat'.
Predicting articles and auxiliaries ('the', 'a', 'are', 'been') after conjunctions, commas and prepositions in flowing descriptive prose.
Predicting 'am'/'pm' right after the hour digit in opening-times strings (and 'co' after the dot in .co.uk web addresses).
Early-layer completion of tight local word pairs from just the immediately preceding token, e.g. 'chow down on', '9am-', 'accession to', 'had your fill of'.
Finishing a word the tokenizer split mid-way ('Cam'->'bridge', 'Sax'->'on', 'amb'->'ience', 'Expl'->'oring'), typically in the earlier part of the window.
Predicting the hyphen of day and month ranges in opening hours - after 'Mon' or 'Apr' - a format the passage has already repeated many times.
Continuing recurring price and address formulas copied from earlier listings: the '/' in 'adult/child', ' £' after 'mains', repeated street names like 'St Margaret's St'.
